entities.summary:
Michael Stryphnos, a Byzantine aristocrat and high-ranking official, rose to prominence during the tumultuous reign of the Angeloi emperors, dying around 1201. As *megas doux* (Grand Duke) of the Byzantine fleet, he wielded significant power in the late 12th century, but his tenure became synonymous with rampant corruption and the catastrophic neglect of the imperial navy. His actions, driven by personal enrichment and factional loyalty, directly contributed to the weakening of the empire's maritime defenses, a vulnerability that would prove fatal just a few years after his death.

Stryphnos secured his influential position through his marriage to Theodora Komnene, a daughter of Emperor Alexios III Angelos's brother, Andronikos Doukas Angelos, solidifying his ties to the ruling dynasty. Appointed *megas doux* by Alexios III, Stryphnos was entrusted with the crucial responsibility of maintaining the Byzantine fleet, a vital strategic asset. Instead, he systematically dismantled ships for timber, sold off equipment, and funneled funds meant for naval upkeep into his own coffers and those of his allies. He appointed unqualified relatives to key positions, further eroding the efficiency and morale of what remained of the once formidable Byzantine navy. His malfeasance was a stark symptom of the wider administrative decay plaguing the Angeloi regime.
